$comment: Curated capability tree for AI agent setups. Like a Civ tech tree, this is authored content: every user gets the same tree and differs only in where they are on it. Nodes are matched against the capabilities discovered in a user's config via `detect` patterns (regex, tested against capability ids). A node with all prerequisites met but nothing detected is what `tt near` and `tt recs` surface as researchable next.

nodes.name: Shell Execution
nodes.description: The agent can run commands and read their output
nodes.hint: Built in to OpenCode

nodes.name: File Editing
nodes.description: The agent can read and modify files directly
nodes.hint: Built in to OpenCode

nodes.name: Code Intelligence
nodes.description: Language-server diagnostics, so the agent sees errors as an IDE would
nodes.hint: Enable LSP for the languages you work in

nodes.name: Version Control
nodes.description: Git operations, so agent work is reviewable and revertible
nodes.hint: Add a git or GitHub MCP server so the agent can branch, diff, and open PRs

nodes.name: Hosted Inference
nodes.description: At least one hosted model provider configured
nodes.hint: Configure a provider with an API key

nodes.name: Local Runtime
nodes.description: A model server running on your own hardware — Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, or LiteRT
nodes.hint: Install Ollama (or llama.cpp / MLX on Apple silicon) and pull one model

nodes.name: Local Tool Calling
nodes.description: A local model that reliably emits tool calls — the threshold where local models stop being chat toys and start doing agent work
nodes.hint: Pull a tool-capable local model (Qwen coder, Hermes, Command-R) and verify it emits tool calls — many local models claim support and fail in practice

nodes.name: Extended Context
nodes.description: A model configured well past the default window, so long files and sessions survive
nodes.hint: Set an explicit context limit per model — most runtimes silently default to 4K and truncate

nodes.name: Model Routing
nodes.description: More than one model available, with agents pinned to the right tier for their work
nodes.hint: Pin cheap models to mechanical subagents and reserve the expensive tier for hard reasoning

nodes.name: Tool Protocol
nodes.description: At least one MCP server, giving the agent capabilities beyond its own context
nodes.hint: Add your first MCP server

nodes.name: Browser Automation
nodes.description: The agent can drive a real browser — see rendered pages, click, and verify its own UI work
nodes.hint: Add a Playwright or browser MCP server so the agent can check its own frontend changes

nodes.name: Web Research
nodes.description: Live search and fetch, so the agent is not limited to its training cutoff
nodes.hint: Add a search or fetch MCP server

nodes.name: Secret Management
nodes.description: Credentials resolved from a vault or env references instead of literals in config
nodes.hint: Move API keys out of opencode.json into a vault or environment references

nodes.name: Data Access
nodes.description: The agent can query real data rather than reasoning about schemas it cannot see
nodes.hint: Connect a database MCP server, ideally read-only to start

nodes.name: Embeddings
nodes.description: Text can be turned into vectors — the prerequisite for any retrieval
nodes.hint: Configure an embedding model; a small local one is usually enough

nodes.name: Vector Store
nodes.description: Somewhere to keep and search those vectors
nodes.hint: Add a vector store — pgvector or a local LanceDB is enough to start

nodes.name: Retrieval
nodes.description: The agent pulls relevant context on demand instead of being handed everything up front
nodes.hint: Wire retrieval into a skill or agent so context is fetched rather than pasted

nodes.name: Persistent Memory
nodes.description: Facts survive between sessions, so the agent stops relearning your setup every time
nodes.hint: Add a memory MCP server or a durable notes file the agent reads on start

nodes.name: Context Compaction
nodes.description: Long sessions summarize instead of falling over at the context limit
nodes.hint: Enable session compaction so long-running work survives the window

nodes.name: Subagents
nodes.description: Named agents with their own prompts and models, delegated to for specific work
nodes.hint: Define your first subagent with a narrow job and its own model

nodes.name: Skill Library
nodes.description: Reusable procedures the agent loads on demand, so expertise is not retyped per session
nodes.hint: Write a SKILL.md for a workflow you explain more than twice

nodes.name: Parallel Execution
nodes.description: Several agents working at once on independent pieces
nodes.hint: Split a broad task across subagents that do not touch the same files

nodes.name: Scheduled Work
nodes.description: Agents that run on a schedule or a trigger, without you starting them
nodes.hint: Move a recurring check onto a schedule instead of remembering to run it

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.description: Long-running work can reach you when it finishes or needs a decision
nodes.hint: Add a push channel so background agents can surface results

nodes.name: Automated Tests
nodes.description: A suite the agent can run to check its own work
nodes.hint: Give the agent a test command it can run unprompted

nodes.name: Review Loop
nodes.description: A second agent checks the first one's output before you see it
nodes.hint: Add a reviewer subagent with a different prompt and a mandate to disagree

nodes.name: Evaluation
nodes.description: Agent output measured against known-good cases rather than judged by vibes
nodes.hint: Collect cases where the agent failed and turn them into a suite you can re-run

nodes.name: Observability
nodes.description: Traces of what agents did, so failures are diagnosable after the fact
nodes.hint: Log agent runs somewhere you can query later

nodes.name: Continuous Delivery
nodes.description: Agent changes ship through the same gate as human ones
nodes.hint: Put agent commits behind CI so nothing merges unverified

nodes.name: Local Embeddings
nodes.description: Retrieval that never sends your text to a third party
nodes.hint: Run the embedding model locally — nomic-embed or bge-small are small enough

nodes.name: Offline Capable
nodes.description: The full loop — inference, tools, retrieval — runs with the network off
nodes.hint: Verify the agent still completes a real task with the network disabled

nodes.name: Private Data Handling
nodes.description: Sensitive material is processed only by models you control
nodes.hint: Route work touching sensitive data to local models by policy, not by habit

nodes.name: Self-Hosted Stack
nodes.description: Your own hardware serving models and tools to your agents
nodes.hint: Move inference onto a machine you own and reach it over a private network
